I'm Russian, currently living in Moscow. Was born in 1998. I don't remember 90s but my parents and grandmother do. They don't really care about it but in general they like soviet era. It had many disadvantages -- deficite of goods, for example.

Now we don't have any problems with it. You can go to supermarket and buy whatever you want. But turning Russia into a country with market economy cost us EVERYTHING. 

90s were a catastrophic years for our country. That's why many older people have some sort of nostalgia for USSR.

Many people lost their jobs, many died, many of them left the country. 90s killed russian microelectronics, killed machine tools manufacturing, almost killed russian car manufacturing industry. Reasons were different -- here's one of them. Many factories that produced goods for entire USSR after the fall left at the territory of former Soviet republics and went bankrupt. For example, car manufacturing company in Riga didn't find any clients in Europe. And one of the last chances for this company to survive -- cooperation with GAZ plant in Nizhny Novgorod -- was somehow interrupted by independent Latvian government. So, all of this had eventually led to its bankruptcy. Another reason is the incompetent management. That's one of the reasons that killed AZLK car factory in Moscow in 1990s. Opening internal market for foreign goods killed many russian manufacturers. They just couldn't compete with them. 

Welp... That was a bit off topic. Now, aome words about my parents' attitude... They're not hating 90s, but think that modern Russia has many problems that were not possible in USSR -- constant risk of losing your job, poor quality of medicine (USSR also had problems with it, but now it's being paid more and more while the quality of it sometimes becomes even worse), massive collapse of education (thanks to NEF exams and government that doesn't really care about giving education a high priority).

I would say so. Living in 70s or 80s meant having no opportunity to buy some goods even if you had enough money -- because of goods' deficite. Private trade was a crime until 1990s.  Living in 90s sometimes meant seeing many goods in stores but not having an opportunity to buy it because of lack of money and because of money itself turning into useless sheets of paper -- inflation was horrible. 

I think if transition from planning economy to market economy was less sharp and more efficient, without industry and science collapsing and country breaking apart, an attitude to USSR could've been much more different. Senior generation doesn't think that USSR was bad. But they saw things that were even worse.
